newsitem.title: UK: Expectation of broad EMU ebbs - JP Morgan index.
newsitem.headline: Expectation of broad EMU ebbs - JP Morgan index.

text.p: Expectations of broad-based economic and monetary union between EU countries other than so-called "core" participants like France and Benelux, have receded over the past 10 days, JP Morgan's EMU expectations calculator shows.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating real-time market expectations of EMU occurring monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.

The latest calculation shows that under this method the market believes there is a 100 percent likelihood of France and Belgium, for example, being in EMU and that assessment is unchanged over the past 10 days.
However, a decline in probability that the UK, Italy and Spain would participate was recorded.

The UK's probability of taking part in EMU dropped six points to 50 percent, Italy's dropped four points to 46 and Spain dropped three poinst to 53. Elsewhere, Denmark fell two points to 34 percent, JP Morgan said.
The calculator shows Sweden is seen to have a 65 percent chance of being in EMU, although this edged lower by one point over the past 10 days.

A market probability level is assigned to each EU country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
